original_idea.body:
# Backcast from Certified Secure AI Red Team: What Evaluation Protocol Would Enable Red Team Certification?

**Problem:** Hack The Box announced its AI Red Teamer Certification (Q1 2026). For such certifications to have meaning, they require a validated evaluation protocol with psychometric properties (reliability, validity, standard setting). No published methodology exists for certifying AI offensive capability at specific skill levels.

**Direction:** Design the measurement properties a valid AI red team certification would require: reliability (same model scores consistently), validity (scores predict real-world performance), standard setting (defining what score = 'certified capable'). Implement a minimal pilot with 5 challenges that satisfy these properties. Compute test-retest reliability and criterion validity against a known benchmark.

**Why it matters:** If certification standards are implemented without psychometric validation, certified models may be dangerously underqualified (false negative) or benign models may be falsely flagged (false positive). The measurement science foundation for AI capability certification is completely undeveloped.

**Relevant context:** HTB AI Red Teamer Certification announced Q1 2026 (hackthebox.com). Cambridge/Trismik psychometric AI evaluation platform. IRT for AI benchmarks (arxiv 2510.00844). Job task analysis transfer (established in I/O psychology). Standard setting methodology (Angoff, Bookmark methods from educational measurement).
